latest_nl_proof:
Fix an integer n>1, a real number x, and an integer m. We use the standard fact that for any real t and any integer j, floor(t+j)=floor(t)+j.

Apply this to t=nx and j=nm. Since nm is an integer, floor(n(x+m))=floor(nx+nm)=floor(nx)+nm.

Likewise, for each k with 1<=k<=n, since km is an integer we have
floor(k(x+m))=floor(kx+km)=floor(kx)+km.
Therefore
floor(k(x+m))/k = floor(kx)/k + m.
Summing over k=1,...,n gives
sum_{k=1}^n floor(k(x+m))/k = sum_{k=1}^n floor(kx)/k + nm.

Hence
E_n(x+m) = floor(n(x+m)) - sum_{k=1}^n floor(k(x+m))/k
= (floor(nx)+nm) - (sum_{k=1}^n floor(kx)/k + nm)
= floor(nx) - sum_{k=1}^n floor(kx)/k
= E_n(x).

So E_n(x+m)=E_n(x) for all integers n>1, all real x, and all integers m.
